questions.body: Which statement correctly contrasts TCP with UDP?

options.text: TCP is connection-oriented and reliable; UDP is connectionless with no delivery guarantee
TCP is faster because it skips acknowledgements

questions.explanation: TCP provides ordered, reliable delivery with flow and congestion control. UDP just sends datagrams, which is why it suits low-latency uses like DNS, games and streaming.
questions.interview_line: Pick TCP when you need correctness and UDP when you need low latency and can tolerate loss.

questions.body: What is the correct order of the TCP three-way handshake?
questions.explanation: The client sends SYN, the server answers SYN-ACK and the client confirms with ACK. Both sides have then agreed initial sequence numbers.
questions.interview_line: The handshake costs one round trip before data can flow, which is why connection reuse matters.

questions.body: At which OSI layer does a router make its forwarding decisions?
questions.explanation: Routers forward IP packets based on destination IP addresses, which is the network layer. Switches work with MAC addresses at the data link layer.
questions.interview_line: Switches forward frames by MAC address, routers forward packets by IP address.

questions.body: Which HTTP methods are defined as idempotent? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Repeating GET, PUT or DELETE leaves the server in the same state as doing it once. POST is not idempotent: repeating it can create several resources.
questions.interview_line: Idempotency is what makes a retry safe, so design write APIs with idempotency keys when you cannot use PUT.

questions.body: The HTTP status code returned when a requested resource does not exist is ____. (Give the number.)
questions.explanation: 404 Not Found means the server cannot find the resource. A 403 means it exists but access is forbidden, and a 401 means authentication is required.
questions.interview_line: Use 4xx for client mistakes and 5xx for server faults.

questions.body: What does a recursive DNS resolver do when it has no cached answer for a name?

options.text: It queries root, then TLD, then authoritative servers and returns the final answer
It asks the client to try again later
It broadcasts the question to the whole subnet
It reads the answer from the client's hosts file

questions.explanation: The resolver walks the hierarchy on behalf of the client and caches the result according to the record's TTL.
questions.interview_line: DNS is a cached, hierarchical lookup, so TTLs decide how fast a change spreads.

questions.body: What does the TLS handshake in HTTPS establish before application data is sent?

options.text: The server's identity (via its certificate) and shared session keys
A permanent connection that never needs closing
A DNS record for the server

questions.explanation: The client verifies the server's certificate chain and both sides derive symmetric keys. After that the data is encrypted and integrity-protected.
questions.interview_line: Asymmetric crypto sets up the session, symmetric crypto carries the data.

questions.body: In TCP slow start, how does the congestion window grow until it reaches the threshold?

options.text: It roughly doubles every round trip
It grows by one segment per round trip

questions.explanation: Each acknowledged segment increases the window by one segment, which doubles it per round trip. After the threshold TCP grows it linearly, and on loss it cuts the window back.
questions.interview_line: TCP probes for bandwidth exponentially, then carefully, and backs off on loss.

questions.body: How many usable host addresses does a /28 IPv4 subnet have? (Give a number.)
questions.explanation: A /28 has 4 host bits, so 16 addresses. The network address and the broadcast address are not usable, leaving 14.
questions.interview_line: Usable hosts are two to the power of host bits, minus two.

options.text: Maps an IP address to a MAC address on the local network
Maps a domain name to an IP address

questions.explanation: A host broadcasts "who has this IP?" and the owner replies with its MAC address, which is cached. DNS maps names to IPs and DHCP assigns addresses.
questions.interview_line: ARP bridges the IP layer and the link layer on one network.

questions.body: NAT lets many devices on a private network share one public IP address by rewriting addresses and ports.
questions.explanation: The NAT device keeps a table mapping each internal address and port to an external port, and rewrites packets in both directions.
questions.interview_line: NAT postponed IPv4 exhaustion but breaks true end-to-end connectivity.

questions.body: A load balancer that routes requests by URL path or HTTP header is working at which kind of layer?
questions.explanation: Reading paths and headers needs the HTTP request, so it is application-layer (L7). An L4 balancer only sees IPs and ports, which makes it faster but less flexible.
questions.interview_line: L4 balancing is cheap and fast; L7 balancing is smarter and costs more per request.
